arxiv-2009-11869.title: Implications of Grain Size Distribution and Composition for the Correlation between Dust Extinction and Emissivity Facilities: Odyssey Cluster, Harvard University ptemcee ( Vousden et al. 2016 ) , emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 ) , NumPy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 )
arxiv-2009-11869.creator: Ioana A. Zelko, Douglas P. Finkbeiner
arxiv-2009-11869.description: Abstract We study the effect of variations in dust size distribution and composition on the correlation between the spectral shape of extinction (parameterized by R V R_{\textnormal{V}} ) and far-infrared dust emissivity (parameterized by the power-law index β \beta ).

arxiv-2103-10195.title: Let-Mi: An Arabic Levantine Twitter Dataset for Misogynistic Language
arxiv-2103-10195.creator: Hala Mulki, Bilal Ghanem
arxiv-2103-10195.description: Abstract Online misogyny has become an increasing worry for Arab women who experience gender-based online abuse on a daily basis. Misogyny automatic detection systems can assist in the prohibition of anti-women Arabic toxic content. Developing such systems is hindered by the lack of the Arabic misogyny benchmark datasets.

arxiv-2304-06113.title: Wiener Indices of Minuscule Lattices
arxiv-2304-06113.creator: Colin Defant, Valentin Féray, Philippe Nadeau, Nathan Williams
arxiv-2304-06113.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Colin Defant, Valentin Féray, Philippe Nadeau, Nathan Williams. The Wiener index of a finite graph G G is the sum over all pairs ( p , q ) (p,q) of vertices of G G of the distance between p p and q q . When P P is a finite poset, we define its Wiener index as the Wiener index of the graph of its Hasse diagram.

arxiv-2409-05561.title: The axioms for right ( n + 𝟐 ) \bm{(n+2)} -angulated categories † † footnotetext: Jing He was supported by the Hunan Provincial Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 2023JJ40217).
arxiv-2409-05561.creator: Jing He, Jiangsha Li
arxiv-2409-05561.description: Abstract Drawing inspiration from the works of Beligiannis–Marmaridis and Lin, we refine the axioms for a right ( n + 2 ) (n+2) -angulated category and give some examples of such categories. Interestingly, we show that the morphism axiom for a right ( n + 2 ) (n+2) -angulated category is actually redundant.

arxiv-2412-05091.title: Designing a Secure, Scalable, and Cost-Effective Cloud Storage Solution: A Novel Approach to Data Management using NextCloud, TrueNAS, and QEMU/KVM
arxiv-2412-05091.creator: Prakash Aryan, Sujala Deepak Shetty
arxiv-2412-05091.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel approach to cloud storage challenges by integrating NextCloud, TrueNAS, and QEMU/KVM. Our research demonstrates how this combination creates a robust, flexible, and economical cloud storage system suitable for various applications. We detail the architecture, highlighting TrueNAS’s ZFS-based storage, QEMU/KVM’s virtualization, and NextCloud’s user interface.

arxiv-2504-17063.title: Port-Hamiltonian modeling of rigid multibody systems
arxiv-2504-17063.creator: Thomas Berger, René Hochdahl, Timo Reis, Robert Seifried
arxiv-2504-17063.description: Abstract We employ a port-Hamiltonian approach to model nonlinear rigid multibody systems subject to both position and velocity constraints. Our formulation accommodates Cartesian and redundant coordinates, respectively, and captures kinematic as well as gyroscopic effects. The resulting equations take the form of nonlinear differential-algebraic equations that inherently preserve an energy balance.

arxiv-2505-14650.title: A model of magnetised and rotating convection for stellar and planetary interiors
arxiv-2505-14650.creator: L. Bessila, S. Mathis
arxiv-2505-14650.description: Abstract Context. Convection is a fundamental mechanism for energy transport in stars and planets, playing a pivotal role in shaping their structures and evolution. The Mixing-Length Theory, a monomodal approach to convection, is widely adopted and implemented in 1D stellar structure and evolution codes.

arxiv-2511-08854.title: Decomposition of Small Transformer Models
arxiv-2511-08854.creator: Casper L. Christensen, Logan Riggs Smith
arxiv-2511-08854.description: Abstract Recent work in mechanistic interpretability has shown that decomposing models in parameter space may yield clean handles for analysis and intervention. Previous methods have demonstrated successful applications on a wide range of toy models, but the gap to "real models" has not yet been bridged.

arxiv-2601-15045.title: Coupled gas and bubble dynamics at the solidification front
arxiv-2601-15045.creator: Bastien Isabella, Cécile Monteux, Sylvain Deville
arxiv-2601-15045.description: Abstract The formation and entrapment of gas bubbles during solidification significantly influence the microstructure and mechanical properties of materials, from metallic alloys to ice. While gas segregation at the solidification front is well-documented, the real-time dynamics of bubble nucleation, growth, and engulfment-and their dependence on solidification velocity-remain poorly understood.

europmc-pmc3441570.title: An integrated pipeline for de novo assembly of microbial genomes.
europmc-pmc3441570.creator: Tritt A, Eisen JA, Facciotti MT, Darling AE.
europmc-pmc3441570.description: Remarkable advances in DNA sequencing technology have created a need for de novo genome assembly methods tailored to work with the new sequencing data types. Many such methods have been published in recent years, but assembling raw sequence data to obtain a draft genome has...

pmc-11548190.title: Biobased Compostable Plastics End-of-Life: Environmental Assessment Including Carbon Footprint and Microplastic Impacts
pmc-11548190.creator: Anthony Keyes, Christopher M Saffron, Shilpa Manjure, Ramani Narayan, Cristina Cazan, Mihaela Cosnita
pmc-11548190.description: In this paper, we examine how traditional life-cycle assessment (LCA) for bio-based and compostable plastics overlooks issues surrounding carbon sequestration and microplastic persistence. To outline biased comparisons drawn from these omitted environmental impacts, we provide, as an example, a comparative LCA for compostable biobased vs. non-compostable fossil-based materials.

pmc-11677728.title: Surface-Functionalizing Strategies for Multiplexed Molecular Biosensing: Developments Powered by Advancements in Nanotechnologies
pmc-11677728.creator: Shangjie Zou, Guangdun Peng, Zhiqiang Ma
pmc-11677728.description: Multiplexed biosensing methods for simultaneously detecting multiple biomolecules are important for investigating biological mechanisms associated with physiological processes, developing applications in life sciences, and conducting medical tests. The development of biosensors, especially those advanced biosensors with multiplexing potentials, strongly depends on advancements in nanotechnologies, including the nano-coating of thin films, micro–nano 3D structures, and nanotags for signal generation.

pmc-12607085.title: Delivering sleep: Bed kit distributions to children living in poverty in Tanzania
pmc-12607085.creator: Debbie Will-Dryden, Wandoa Mwambu, Teegan Nordstrom, Reut Gruber
pmc-12607085.description: BackgroundOvercrowded housing, insufficient beds, and poor mosquito protection are major barriers to healthy sleep for children living in poverty in developing countries. This study aimed to address these barriers by providing children living in poverty in Tanzania with climate-appropriate items essential for creating a safe and comfortable micro-sleep environment.

pmc-12830625.title: Altered PTPN13–β-catenin interaction by pathogenic mutations and involvement of this axis in B-cell receptor signalling
pmc-12830625.creator: David A Cabrera-Riofrío, Hongbing Li, Clara García-Calvo, Carmen Sánchez-Bernal, Jesús Sánchez-Yagüe, Yigal Dror, Rubén M Buey, Ángel Hernández-Hernández
pmc-12830625.description: Protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 13 (PTPN13) is a non-receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase with context-dependent roles as tumour suppressor or promoter. Its modular structure supports multiple molecular interactions, including a critical one with β-catenin, a regulator of the haematopoietic system.

pmc-13375172.title: Determinants of Formula Feeding among Mothers in Indonesia: The Role of Digital Media and Microeconomic Factors
pmc-13375172.creator: Nur Khasanah, Riska Herliana, Alva Cherry Mustamu, Anita Liliana, Endah Tri Wahyuni, Maria Sriana Banul, Nur Hafni Hasim
pmc-13375172.description: Background:Maternal decision-making regarding the use of infant formula milk in Indonesia is shaped by a complex interplay of social, economic, and informational factors. This study aimed to elucidate the determinants of mothers’ choices when selecting formula milk in Sorong City, Indonesia, addressing gaps in previous research that overlooked the role of digital media and microeconomic factors in maternal decision-making.

pmc-13376520.title: Tau T205 phosphorylation modulates engram cell recruitment and remote memory in mice
pmc-13376520.creator: Renée Kosonen, Kristie Stefanoska, Yijun Lin, Samantha Edwards, Emmanuel Prikas, Josefine Bertz, Anne Poljak, Lars M Ittner, Arne Ittner
pmc-13376520.description: Memory loss is linked to failure of the engram, the physical substrate associated with a specific memory. Tau is a microtubule associated protein best known for its central role in neurodegenerative dementias, yet its physiological function in memory formation remains poorly understood. In this work, we show that tau is crucial for forming long lasting memories in mice.

pmc-13449541.title: Human Papillomavirus DNA and p16 Expression in Oral and Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Cross-Sectional Clinicopathologic Study in Western India
pmc-13449541.creator: Hardik Jain, Ashish Surana, Sudha Jain, Akruti Patel, Gunjan Jain
pmc-13449541.description: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma is biologically and clinically distinct from conventional tobacco- and alcohol-related head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Indian data remain heterogeneous because oral cavity and oropharyngeal tumors are often analyzed together despite their different etiologic patterns.

pmc-13649604.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of hematopoietic and non-hematopoietic cells defines a distinct signature in atopic and NRG1 mouse lung
pmc-13649604.creator: Yingjie Li, Ahmed Ghobashi, Syed-Rehan A. Hussain, Michelle Rohlfing, Jennifer Santoro, Matthew S. Bochter, Shin-ichi Abe, Qin Ma, Mitchell H. Grayson
pmc-13649604.description: Respiratory viral infections cause significant mortality. Pre-existing atopy has demonstrated protection from virus-induced death. Atopic mice with house dust mite (HDM) extract survive normally lethal parainfluenza (Sendai virus, SeV) and influenza A (IAV) infection. Neuregulin-1 (NRG1), markedly elevated in airways of atopic mice, has been shown to significantly attenuate mortality to SeV and IAV in non-atopic mice.
